subject: POC plan: model recommendations, structured-output schema, and compliance tests
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lim <sara@nimbusretail.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Jul 2026 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps & checklist for POC - model selection + output schema

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can move toward a scoped POC:

Recap from discovery:
- Primary integration: product enrichment + store-level price lookup for product pages (JSON product object supplied by Nimbus).
- Volume: ~200 QPS peak (primarily reads at 95th), average 35 QPS. Bursty at catalog sync times.
- Latency target: 95th < 300ms for the text-generation path used for structured product enrichment; fallback ok at 600ms.
- Quality concerns: hallucinations on numeric attributes (price, availability) and schema drift when product descriptions are long.
- Security: PII not stored; data residency US-only.

What we recommend for the 2-week POC:
1) Model candidates to evaluate (we'll pre-provision):
   - Llama2-13B-chat (quantized, 8-bit) — good starting point for structured output fidelity vs cost.
   - Mistral-7B-instruct (quantized) — lower cost, strong on instruction following for short prompts.
   - Redwood-curated 6B-retrieval (prod-variant) — latest runtime optimizations for KV cache-heavy workloads (we'll include a latency profile).

2) Structured output approach:
   - Primary output: strict JSON object validated against a JSON Schema (we'll enforce schema on the service side).
   - On schema non-compliance: return a deterministic error payload with an error_code and minimal text fallback.
   - Tool/function calls: we recommend using the function-calling surface for external lookups (e.g., price_lookup(product_id) => returns canonical price and timestamp). Include idempotency tokens for retries.
   - Retry rules: for transient runtime errors retry up to 2x with exponential backoff; for schema-validation failures do NOT retry automatically (requires prompt adjustment).

3) Eval plan and artifacts we'll provide:
   - Prompt set v1 (attached): ~120 prompts covering attribute extraction, enumeration constraints, malformed descriptions, and long-text truncation cases.
   - Benchmark CSV (attached): latency and token-cost simulation for baseline throughput.
   - Eval harness link: shared Drive + HubSpot record for tracking (link below).

4) Next steps / asks from Nimbus:
   - Share a small sample of product JSON (5–10 records) and an example of the worst-case product description.
   - Confirm the SSO contact for contract routing (procurement email in CC looks right).
   - Authorize us to run a short synthetic workload (read-only) against a staging endpoint for 2 hours during initial provisioning window.

I'll kick off provisioning once you confirm the sample data and sign the PO/DocuSign when ready. Proposed next call: Thu Jul 9 10:00am PT to review initial runs.

Attachments: redwood_promptset_v1.jsonl, benchmark_summary_20260706.csv

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124

[Attachment stubs: redwood_promptset_v1.jsonl (120 prompts), benchmark_summary_20260706.csv (latency/cost sim)]

From: Sara Lim <sara@nimbusretail.com>

Cc: Eric Cole <eric.cole@nimbusretail.com>, Nimbus Retail (procurement) <procurement@nimbusretail.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Jul 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps & checklist for POC - model selection + output schema

Laura —

Appreciate the clear summary. Quick answers and attachments:
- Attached a small product sample (nimbus_product_sample.csv) with a couple of long descriptions and some legacy SKUs.
- Procurement: procurement@nimbusretail.com will handle the DocuSign/PO.
- Concern: our stack currently validates downstream JSON strictly; if the model returns a slightly different shape we break our pipeline. Can you outline how Redwood will gate schema-violations prior to production routing?
- Cost sensitivity: prefer starting with the smaller model if latency/quality is acceptable.

We can do Thu Jul 9 at 10:00am PT. Please include whoever owns the eval harness on your side.

Thanks,
Sara Lim
Head of Product Integrations | Nimbus Retail
[sara@nimbusretail.com]

[Attachment: nimbus_product_sample.csv (12 rows)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2026 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: POC plan from Nimbus - need infra + eval owner

Team —

Forwarding Nimbus product sample and their schema concerns. Proposed internal plan:
- Neha: own eval harness and structured-output tests (JSON Schema conformance + fuzz tests). Use the promptset attached and include a batch of injected malformed descriptions. Measure strict_conformance_rate and mean_time_to_fix (MTTF) for failures.
- Vivek: provision a dedicated instance for the 2-week POC (start with Mistral-7B and Llama2-13B quantized variants). Ensure region us-west and US-only data residency. Add automatic fallback route to the smaller model on high latency conditions.
- Rishi: prepare a short runbook for function-calling retries and idempotency token patterns we will recommend to the customer; include example code snippet for price_lookup and handling of transient errors.

Goals for internal kickoff: have the eval harness running and first batch results by Thu morning before the joint call. Also create a small smoke test that validates schema compliance (fail fast).

Is everyone ok with the responsibilities? If yes I will confirm with Nimbus and schedule the call.

Laura

Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC kickoff + links (eval harness + scheduling)

Hi Sara / team —

Thanks — we stood up the eval harness and ran an initial batch against the promptset you received. Highlights:
- Strict schema compliance (first pass)
  - Llama2-13B-chat (8-bit): 88% strict_conformance_rate, mean latency 290ms (95th 420ms).
  - Mistral-7B-instruct (8-bit): 81% strict_conformance_rate, mean latency 210ms (95th 360ms).
  - Redwood-curated 6B-optimized: 84% strict_conformance_rate, mean latency 240ms (95th 380ms).

Known failure modes observed in the initial run: nested arrays for attributes sometimes returned as strings; numeric fields (price) occasionally formatted with currency symbols. We've encoded post-processing rules in the harness to flag and classify these failures so we can craft targeted prompts.

Actions we completed and links:
- Eval harness (read-only): https://drive.redwood.com/shared/NIMPOC-eval-harness
- Initial report: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/NIMPOC-eval-harness/report-20260708.pdf
- HubSpot record: HS-987654 (I added the POC tasks and Milestones).

Proposed joint agenda for Thu Jul 9 10:00am PT:
1) Review initial strict_conformance_rate and failure clusters (10m)
2) Walkthrough of function-calling pattern for price_lookup + retry semantics (10m)
3) Plan targeted prompt adjustments and guardrail examples (10m)
4) Confirm contract/procurement timeline (5m)

If that works I will send a calendar invite and include the quick runbook for retries.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124
